findings.observation: SourceGuard serializes finish flag/native owner-count bookkeeping, each wait predicate check/native unlock, and frequency cache/QPC access through one immutable Execution owner. The gate releases before Sleep and optional publication observer. Windows LastError is preserved by gate bookkeeping. Recovered MutexState layout remains unchanged; Execution source layout is extended.

Header excludes a second Execution sharing the same referenced state, direct helpers/public predicate or plain outside concurrent reads/writes, and Platform lock/QPC reentry or unknown throwing outcomes. Error5 and unlock-exception tests retain observed partial native write/count prefixes without invented unlock, rollback, safe retry or publication.

Milestones begins with zero bits, binds one exact Execution issuer and three distinct flag cells, and cannot reset/rebind. finish flag maps exact first/second/third storage to Server/Online/Libraries; unrelated supplied flag still writes but emits no event. Host event is after normal host return and before attachment completion. fetch_or acq_rel and acquire all-bit observation publish the initial prefixes; issuer mismatch/invalid stage poison readiness.

bind_foreign creates one owned Milestones and one foreign Domain, refuses replacing existing observer/attachment, checks the actual callback view Execution identity, and retains observer/provider owners. Resources lifetime covers the Execution raw observer. The unchanged external hook-quiescence proof remains distinct from source readiness.

Source milestones are initial-data prefix completion, not worker completion, hook success, server health, PTD quiescence or join. Server publishes port before async_accept/run_context and remains live in the integration test. Online/Libraries may still perform bootstrap/native thread exit cleanup after finish. Host engine-init failure can return normally and emit Host; the remaining provider proof rejects activation in that case.

Core uses own real SRW/thread metadata to test wait-sleep release, eight concurrent clock readers with one cache initialization, observer waiting for another Execution call after both gates release, exact mapping/failure prefix and cross-thread plain-payload release/acquire. Integration invokes actual source workers on own threads with controlled providers; a held own server run_context coexists with later source milestones and sequential foreign callbacks. No original/rebuilt DLL/game, real hook/registry/socket/process/UI or foreign module is executed.

Resources gains an optional shared publication owner and Execution gains a source mutex/observer and is explicitly noncopyable/nonmovable. All consumers must rebuild. Quick capture refreshes Execution/backend and Resources by-value factory/host binder consumers; nine frozen source hashes and both EXE hashes match. Before/after changes match four baseline sources;791 other tracked sources are identical.

limitations: Synchronization covers one Execution instance and its referenced state only; it is not a process-global registry or protection for arbitrary direct helper/plain-state callers.

OS lock/QPC boundaries must not reenter or throw unknown outcomes. Recursive mutex does not make arbitrary native SRW reentry safe; partial native error state does not become retryable when the source guard releases.
Publication is optional nonthrowing bookkeeping, not worker-side controller activation. Foreign activation remains an explicit controller call after all source bits and mandatory remaining proof.
All bits attest initial source prefixes only. Server work/health, worker exit cleanup, PTD/RO/FLS teardown, actual hook success and worker joins remain separate.
Provider/stream/fallback ownership, later shared state mutation, PTD policy, actual hook-disabled/cached-entry quiescence and native unload/CRT/EH/ABI/PE equivalence remain required.

Sequential foreign callback support and overlap/reentry rejection remain B18 scope; general concurrent callback success is not added.7online foreign calls,configuration/license/legacy document and B10 historical review debt remain open.
